chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Trading in the Conn at Manny's and trying the Selmer
summary: He got a Selmer and Otto Link mouthpiece; the new horn sounded distant until he got used to it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x:
Went down to Manny's and the Selmers
had came in. And Manny said, "Give me that Conn horn,
I'll trade you."

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I say, "Look, we got a drive on (inaudible)."
Say, "I'll trade you -- I'll give you a Selmer, you give me the Conn."
"And we'll trade. I'll give you a good break on the Conn."
And Selmer was like a hundred and some dollars. Now today, it's about a thousand or twelve hundred, you know.
And I got two guys who want to buy it. I wouldn't sell it for nothing, you know.
So what happened -- I say, "Okay."
Now I get the Selmer. I get an Otto Link mouthpiece. He fixed the Link mouthpiece up for me, I get the Selmer.
And I'm upstairs and I'm playing the thing and it sounds good. I'm in the room back there, I put my mouthpiece on and it sounds good to me. I say, "Oh, this is nice."
Now, when I got to work that night, the band hit up. And I break out in sweats because now I'm playing a new horn. I can't hear the horn.
I'm just playing but it ain't the sound

that I'm getting out of the Conn. See, the Conn you hear it all around you. You know, loud. When I play the Selmer, I don't hear the horn.
The horn sound goes away from you. It comes back --
(Inaudible).
(Inaudible) It's out front.
So, I'm playing the horn and I say, "Man," --
Taft say, "You'll get used to it, you'll get used to it. It sounds good."
I say, "I can't hear this thing, man."
Taft say, "Yeah, it sounds good. What do you mean you can't hear it?"
"You ain't got used to the sound." He kept telling me, "You ain't got used to the sound."
And whatchamacallem say, "Yeah, it sounds" -- (Inaudible) say, "It sounds all right."
Because I think Hilton was using the the alto.
(Inaudible).
Yeah. Hilton was using --

Hilton and Chauncey and all those guys were playing the Selmer -- alto.
(Inaudible) tenor. When I got used to it, oh! I'd go up there one afternoon and I was playing this horn, the guy say, "Hey, man, I heard you way downstairs. That thing sure" --
"What're you playing? You got a Selmer?" I say, "Yeah." I say, "Man, it's been beating."
He say, "I was standing back in the back and hear you just as plain as day. He say the sound carries a lot, you know. The horn is like a violin. It carries -- it's good.
